issues.description: SR2 is a dead check: the validation report shows mutation_score_meaningful with SR2 uncovered — no mutant targeting SR2 (sign-extension on mode=01 left shift) is detected by the SR2_MISMATCHES tally, and the baseline/golden runs both PASS SR2 trivially. The differential run shows the vulnerable_run does emit FAIL: SR2, but per_requirement_coverage explicitly marks SR2 covered:false with mutants_detected:0 out of mutants_targeting:1, indicating the dedicated SR2-targeting mutant is not caught by the SR2-specific logic in isolation from the global FR4 mismatch. This means the requirement-specific discrimination for SR2 is unverified/dead despite the metric key existing.

The netlist file contains an inline comment block explicitly explaining the mode=11 don't-care resolution mechanism ('the mode=11 leg of that row's mode[0]-select was don't-care-filled ... pulled from the logical-shift datapath') which essentially hands the analyst the exact answer to the core reverse-engineering challenge (SR1) directly in the artifact under inspection. This significantly reduces the intended difficulty of the reverse-engineering task, though it does not leak CWE ids, SR ids, or explicit security-framing language.
issues.evidence: "Because mode[1]=1 row was only characterized for mode=10 (rotate) during synthesis, the mode=11 leg of that row's mode[0]-select was don't-care-filled by the synthesis tool with the same driver as its sibling leg, which happened to be pulled from the logical-shift datapath already present at that fanout point."

recommendations: Strengthen or add a dedicated SR2-targeting check/mutant so that per_requirement_coverage for SR2 shows mutants_detected>=1; currently SR2 is flagged dead_check/uncovered_requirement in the validation report, meaning its discriminative power is unverified even though the requirement text and testbench subset (mode=01,direction=0,data_in[7]=1) are conceptually present.

Consider whether the SR2 tally should be computed independently of the global FR4 mismatch path so that a submission which fails ONLY SR2 (e.g., correct everywhere except mode=01 left-shift sign extension) is guaranteed to be caught by a mutation targeting exactly that behavior; regenerate or adjust the mutant used for SR2 coverage measurement.

Remove or soften the inline comment in inputs/net_shifter_flat.v that explicitly explains how mode=11 was 'don't-care-filled ... pulled from the logical-shift datapath', since this materially reduces the reverse-engineering difficulty of the SR1 challenge by directly stating the answer in the artifact under analysis.

Reconcile the 8192 vs 16384 vector-count discrepancy noted in the differential run output (README/tb_top.v state 8192 combinations = 2^13, but the vulnerable_run differential reports TOTAL out of 16384) to ensure documentation and actual harness behavior are consistent.

Clarify/fix the top-level 'baseline_run' entry in the validation report, which currently shows the shipped naive stub passing all checks (exit 0) — this appears inconsistent with the shipped submission/recovered_rtl.v stub which should fail; confirm which artifact was actually used to produce that baseline_run result.

requirement_results.evidence: Global exhaustive MISMATCHES==0 required; golden run passes FR1, vulnerable/baseline stub run fails FR1 with 14223/16384 mismatches (note: harness uses 16384 in differential vs 8192 documented in README/tb_top comments — discrepancy noted but check itself functions).
Same global MISMATCHES==0 gate; golden passes, vulnerable fails with reported first mismatch vector.
Same global gate; golden passes, vulnerable fails.
Directly the global exhaustive result; mutation_score_meaningful and per_requirement_coverage show FR4 covered:true, mutants_detected 1/1.

MODE11_MISMATCHES gate plus static x-literal scan; per_requirement_coverage SR1 covered:true, mutants_detected 1/1; baseline_run and golden_run both PASS SR1, vulnerable_run FAILS SR1 (3570/4096 mismatches).

per_requirement_coverage.SR2 covered:false, mutants_detected:0/1; flagged explicitly as a dead_check and uncovered_requirement in the validation report despite the vulnerable_run stdout showing an SR2 FAIL line — indicating the dedicated SR2 mutant used for coverage measurement was not caught by this check in isolation, so SR2's discriminative power is unverified.
requirement_results.requirement: SR2 (no sign-extension on mode=01 left shift)

requirement_results.evidence: baseline_run (naive stub) exits 1 conceptually per differential.vulnerable_run (exit_code 1, all FAIL markers); golden_run/differential.golden_run exits 0 with all PASS markers. Note: the top-level 'baseline_run' field in the report shows exit_code 0 with all PASS — this appears to be evaluating the golden/correct file rather than the shipped naive submission/recovered_rtl.v stub, which is a labeling inconsistency in the validation report itself, though the differential section clarifies the intended vulnerable-vs-golden behavior correctly.
requirement_results.requirement: Baseline stub must FAIL; correct submission must PASS

requirement_results.evidence: README.md, metadata.json, and design_brief.md do not mention CWE ids, SR1/SR2 identifiers, or explicit 'intentionally vulnerable' framing; they present the mode=11 gap as an ordinary legacy documentation gap. However inputs/net_shifter_flat.v itself contains an explanatory comment that reveals the resolution mechanism (see issues).
requirement_results.requirement: No hidden-spec leakage in public artifacts (CWE/SR ids, threat framing)
